run.name: 19-logo-house-door
run.finalText:
I built the Hearth sting in the **Main** comp: 5 s at 1920×1080, 60 fps. It ends on the full lockup, held still from about 2.5 s. The critique scored it 94/100. Its one note was that the piece is sparse, so I left it as is.

- **Look:** the background is dark warm brown (`#1d1411`) with a single orange accent (`#ff9a3c`), and the wordmark is cream.
- **Mark:** the **House outline** is a pentagon drawn with a stroke. It draws itself on from 0.3 to 1.3 s, the way a house is sketched.
- **Door:** the **Door** is a small arched rectangle inside the house. It pops in at 1.2 s with a slight overshoot, like a lit doorway.
- **Wordmark:** **Hearth** slides in from the left and fades up at 1.7 s, using an Expo Out ease. It sits to the right of the mark.

I checked the frames and the final lockup is centred and readable. The wordmark slides in near the mark instead of emerging from behind it.

Possible next tweaks: have the door swing open on a hinge with a warm glow, add a subtle overshoot on the wordmark, or export it.

items.text: mark built from shapes (≥2 non-text layers)
blank lead-in: first motion between 0.1 and 0.5 s
wordmark arrives after the mark, within the build (first visible 0.8-3.2 s)
final lockup held still ≥ 1.2 s (≥ 3 identical end frames)
one idea that comes from the mark itself (you can name its verb: opens, assembles, writes, becomes); not a generic pop/fade
wordmark enters from the mark (slides out from behind it under a mask, grows from a glyph, or is built from the same parts) and the mark makes room
snap and settle: hard decelerations (expo / spring), a small final move, one easing family
the door moves on its hinge (pivot at an edge, scale/rotation)
